name: Edison Award Silver - Applied Technology
summary: Won Silver Edison Award in Applied Technology category for AI-powered patent search innovation.
description: Recognized in the prestigious Edison Awards 2019 for developing Catalyst, an AI-powered patent search platform. Catalyst enables researchers and inventors to tap into the vast, but underutilized and difficult to comprehend, knowledge existing in patents and gather ideas on how to devise better solutions and products faster. The tool obviates the need for researchers to gain legal expertise to search and understand patents written in a convoluted manner.

name: US Patent Granted - AI/ML Innovation
summary: Granted US patent for innovative method to identify objectives from patent documents using machine learning.
description: Granted United States Patent for a novel method and system for identifying objectives from patent documents using machine learning and natural language processing. The invention presents an innovative approach to automatically extract and identify key objectives from complex patent texts, significantly improving patent analysis efficiency and accuracy. This patented work demonstrates advanced capabilities in AI/ML, particularly in applying statistical significance analysis and feature engineering to legal document processing. The patent includes 19 claims protecting the innovative methodology for automated objective identification in patent documents.

patent_details.title: Method and system to identify objectives from patent documents
patent_details.abstract: A method and a system for identifying an objective from documents is disclosed. In some embodiment, the method includes determining a correlation of each of a plurality of keywords extracted from a set of documents with respect to each class within a set of predefined classes. The method further includes determining a first set of keywords from the plurality of keywords. The method further includes identifying a set of data samples comprising a first plurality of sentences and a second plurality of sentences. The method further includes computing a statistical significance value of each keyword in the first set of keywords with respect to the first plurality of sentences. The method further includes generating a first set of features by discarding at least one keyword from the first set of keywords. The method further includes training a machine learning model to identify an objective of a document.

name: Introduction to LangGraph - LangChain Academy
summary: Completed comprehensive LangGraph course covering agentic and multi-agent applications, state management, and production deployment.
description: Successfully completed the official LangChain Academy course on LangGraph - a framework for building agentic and multi-agent applications. The comprehensive 6-hour course covered 54 lessons across 6 modules, including graph fundamentals, state and memory management, human-in-the-loop workflows, parallelization, long-term memory, and production deployment strategies. LangGraph is a low-level, controllable orchestration framework for complex agentic systems, providing better precision and control compared to traditional agent frameworks. This certification demonstrates proficiency in building production-ready AI agents with advanced features like streaming, breakpoints, sub-graphs, and the LangGraph Platform.

name: Generative AI with Large Language Models
summary: Completed comprehensive course on generative AI fundamentals, LLM training, fine-tuning, and deployment taught by AWS AI practitioners.
description: Successfully completed the Generative AI with Large Language Models course by DeepLearning.AI and AWS on Coursera. This course provided foundational knowledge and practical skills on how generative AI works, covering the complete LLM lifecycle from pre-training to fine-tuning and deployment. Learned cutting-edge techniques including instruction fine-tuning, RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback), parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), and model optimization strategies. The course featured instruction from expert AWS AI practitioners who actively build and deploy AI in real-world business use cases, providing insights into how companies create value with generative AI technology.

name: LangChain for LLM Application Development
summary: Learned LangChain framework directly from creator Harrison Chase, covering RAG, agents, memory, and building production LLM applications.
description: Successfully completed the LangChain for LLM Application Development course by DeepLearning.AI, taught directly by Harrison Chase, the creator of the LangChain framework. This hands-on course covered essential concepts for building production LLM applications including applying LLMs to proprietary data, building personal assistants and specialized chatbots, and implementing advanced patterns like Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Learned to use agents for dynamic tool selection, chained calls for complex workflows, and memory systems to maintain context across conversations. The course provided practical experience in expanding LLM use cases beyond simple prompt-response patterns to create sophisticated, context-aware AI applications.
